newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash grades strengthen on bullish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash grades strengthen on bullish sentiment.

text.p: Stronger contracts for differences (CFD's) values bolstered U.S. cash crude grade differentials Friday morning, pushing Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James barrels into firmer territory.
At the same time grades gained, outright crude prices slipped slightly on NYMEX technical selling.
Extreme price advances from Thursday were clipped, leaving June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing around 5 cents lower at $20.25-35 a barrel.
LLS/St. James was sold at 7-8 cents over June WTI/Cushing, around 5-6 cents stronger than Thursday.
Midland/WTI sold at WTI/Cushing -31 cents, steady from deals confirmed Thursday.
Other grades saw West Texas Sour/Midland steady at $1.50-45 under the benchmark, and Eugene Island at a wide $1.50-35 discount.
Sweet grades were benefitting from the lack of North Sea Brent offerings in the U.S. Gulf, and less economic terms for briging over foreign barrels.
Brent has become a more attractive play for Far East destinations with the sharp turn in Brent-Dubai spreads.
WTI/Cushing Postings were at $1.95-1.99, tracking the June/July roll whch stood at plus 3-7 cents.
